sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Pseudovirus entry assay (MLV pseudoviruses and WNV VLPs carrying GFP reporter): Myc-tagged hTIM1-expressing 293T cells showed increased viral entry compared to hACE2-expressing controls, demonstrating that the N-terminally Myc-tagged construct is functionally active on the cell surface (L2). Cell surface expression of the tagged construct was confirmed in stable HEK293T lines (L3).
sites.rationale: HAVCR1/TIM-1 is a type-I single-pass transmembrane protein with signal peptide at residues 1–20 and a single extracellular domain spanning residues 21–295; the only extracellular terminus is the mature N-terminus beginning at S21. The published construct replaces the endogenous SP with a heterologous SP followed immediately by the Myc tag and then the mature TIM-1 sequence, placing the tag at insert_after_residue=20 in canonical numbering (residue_before=G, residue_after=S). Python verification confirms seq[19]='G' and seq[20]='S', and the insert site is 275 residues from the TM boundary (296), well clear of the ≥3-residue minimum. Three independent ledger lines (L1, L2, L3) all describe this same construct, with L2 providing functional validation via pseudovirus entry and L3 confirming stable cell-surface expression. L1/L3: Full-length hTIM1 (without its own signal peptide) was cloned into a retroviral vector downstream of a heterologous signal peptide (mouse ACE2 SP) and an N-terminal Myc tag, producing a membrane-anchored construct. Stable HEK293T cell lines expressing hTIM1, rhTIM1, and mTIM1 with the Myc tag at their N-terminus were generated and confirmed to be expressed on the cell surface (L3). The tag is placed at the mature N-terminus of the protein; in canonical UniProt numbering this corresponds to insert_after_residue=20 (after the endogenous signal peptide cleavage site, residues 1–20), with the mature chain beginning at S21. This is the only extracellular terminus of the type-I single-pass topology, so the position is uniquely determined.

sources.claim: HEK293T cells stably expressing hTIM1, rhTIM1, or mTIM1 (hTIM1-293T, rhTIM1-293T, and mTIM1-293T, respectively) with the MYC tag at their N-terminus, were generated.

literature_notes: All three ledger lines (L1, L2, L3) converge on a single site: the extracellular mature N-terminus of HAVCR1 (after SP cleavage at residue 20). No ledger line describes an internal loop insertion or a C-terminal (intracellular) tag. The C-terminus of HAVCR1 is intracellular (residues 317–364) and is therefore not a surface-tag site. No transposon, FP-fusion, or domain-insertion screen data are present in the ledger for internal extracellular loop sites. The position is classified topology_derived because none of the three clips explicitly names a residue number at the junction; the mature N-terminus is the unique extracellular terminus and the position follows deterministically from the landmarks.
